whatItDoes: Research a topic across the web, grade and revise the write-up against an editorial rubric, illustrate it, then build and deploy a live report site. Reads the top sources in full, self-critiques the draft before it publishes, and can map the result onto a subdomain you own.
longDescription: Give it a topic. It plans a couple of search queries, dedupes sources, reads the survivors in full, and has a model write a cited report. A second model grades it against a fixed editorial bar and revises if it falls short. It generates an illustration or two, then hands the package to a coding agent that builds and deploys a self-contained static site, returning a URL. `mapDomain` points a domain you own at it, and `dryRun` stops once the report clears self-critique.
notes:
Click **Use this template**. Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it.

Give it a `topic` (what to research) and, optionally, an `audience` to tune the tone. `reviewThreshold` (default 0.7) and `maxDraftAttempts` (default 2) control the self-critique loop. `illustrationCount` (default 2, max 3) controls how many sections get a generated image; set it to 0 to skip illustration entirely. To publish under your own domain, register or own the domain in Sapiom first, then pass `customDomain` (a domain you own) and an optional `subdomain` (defaults to `www`) to add a CNAME to the live site. Leave the domain off and you still get a shareable preview URL. Pass `dryRun: true` to get the report back after self-critique, without illustrating, building, or deploying anything.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` and `{ "topic": "...", "dryRun": true }` to trace plan, gather, synthesize, and critique, and read the report (capabilities stubbed, nothing built), or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.
